Hi Jill,

First-time renting in Japan feels overwhelming to everyone.

About the utilities: for a one-person apartment, budget roughly 10,000 to
20,000 yen a month all in (electricity, gas and water together around 8,000
to 15,000, a little more in peak summer and winter, plus home internet at
around 4,000 to 5,000).

Now the part that shapes everything. Going unfurnished does open more
choice and a lower monthly rent, but in Japan it comes with real strings:

Key money (reikin) often one month and non-refundable, on top of a deposit,
agency fee and guarantor company fee. Move-in

That is possibly an option.  But she would incur those same fees once she moves to unfurnished apartment from her furnished apartment correct?
Course is a year and a half.  From what I can see the nearest train station is Takadanobaba station.
My current currency is American dollars if you send quote.  
Thank you!

Hi Jill, Great question, and you are right to ask. Yes, if she moved from a
furnished place into an unfurnished lease later, she would pay the
unfurnished move-in costs again at that point, so the two-step approach
only really pays off for long stays. For an 18-month stay, two cleaner
options: 1. Stay in a furnished or monthly place for the whole period. No
key money, no guarantor, flexible, cat-friendly, and one modest setup
instead of two. It costs a bit more per month, but you avoid duplicate
move-in fees and the arrival-day risk entirely. 2. Go straight into one

manages each option.
